thread:
incident-bot: PAGER: severity=P1 rdma-fabric->serving-runtime errors detected on pool-eta. auto-escalate to #incidents. Affected: 3 nodes flapping, multiple container restarts. Pager: infra-oncall

Alice Zhang: I'm on it. seeing a bunch of `CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY` and container restarts on pods in pool-eta. nodes: node-rw-17-3, node-rw-17-4, node-rw-18-1.

Ben Khan: confirming. logs from pod redwood-13b-q4-5f8d:
```
2026-03-15T02:03:12Z ERROR runtime: allocation failed: CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY
2026-03-15T02:03:12Z WARN serving: kv cache miss spikes, retransmit errors observed
2026-03-15T02:03:13Z INFO network: rdma retransmit 482 -> rnr_nak_count high
```

Max Keller: net telemetry: infra switch r17-s2 shows port flaps, rx errors rising. tcpdump/ib stats show heavy packet drops and reorders. rack-17 interconnect has ~40-60% packet loss per flow. suspect link-level issue between top-of-rack and spine.

Anya Reyes: customer-impact: Support report INC-4591, three tenants report 500s and long tail latency (~10s). CS already warned large customers. No data exfil.

Ben Khan: quick mitigation suggestions:
- throttle batch_size to 1 and reduce max_output_tokens to 256 for affected model route
- disable prefix KV caching for pool-eta instances to reduce mem pressure
- spin up fallback pool in us-west-2 and shift 30% traffic there (canary)
- cordon/drain the most flappy nodes

Alice Zhang: doing the drain + config now. running:
```
kubectl get pods -n serving -o wide | grep pool-eta
kubectl cordon node-rw-17-3
kubectl drain node-rw-17-3 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=5m
# update runtime config to reduce batching
curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN' https://platform.internal/api/runtime/config -d '{"pool":"pool-eta","batch_size":1,"max_tokens":256,"kv_cache":false}'
```

support-bot: Noted. CS notified customers with interim mitigation steps and ETA of 30m for partial remediation.

incident-bot: handoff: Alice -> Max (infra-oncall) at 02:08Z.

Max Keller: taking over. I'll open net ticket to datacenter team and coordinate port reset on r17-s2. Also requesting graceful fallback routing: set route policy for pool-eta to prefer us-west-2:0.7->us-east-1:0.3. Applying in route-manager.

Ben Khan: while we wait for hardware, I recommend temporary runtime flag to force single-gpu inference (no multi-node) for the affected model to avoid cross-node KV syncs. Command:
```
POST /v1/admin/models/redwood-13b-q4/override
{ "single_gpu_only": true }
```

Max Keller: net team rebooted switch port, link error counters dropped rapidly. observing fewer retransmits. re-enabled KV cache on one node to test stability.

Alice Zhang: after drain and routing changes, 5xx rate dropped from 5.2% -> 0.9% over 10m, p95 latency down from 2.5s -> 0.9s. still monitoring.

Anya Reyes: CS update sent to impacted customers: incident summary + mitigation + timeline.

Max Keller: leaving follow-up actions:
- network oncall to investigate flaky optics on r17-s2 (ticket NET-5821)
- run burn-in on replaced port for 4h
- postmortem with timeline and RCA, include model routing fallback playbook update
- verify KV cache telemetry and add alert for sustained rnr_nak_count > 100/min

Alice Zhang: agreed. I will keep thread open for 2h and then escalate to postmortem if flaps resume. thumbs up for now :thumbsup:

support-bot: Monitoring channel set to high fidelity and retention increased for this thread. Logs and timeline archived to /incidents/archives/2112233445 for postmortem.

incident-bot: Incident severity downgraded to P2 at 02:22Z, still in monitoring.

Max Keller: closing active mitigation. if anyone sees recurrence ping me directly.
